Access.description: What a profile may do, from least to most.

AgentConfig.description: Limits on what a coding agent can get, under `[agent]`.

auto_revoke.description:
Whether `fob exec` mints a Cloudflare token for each command an
agent runs and deletes it when the command ends, as `--revoke` does.

max_ttl.description:
The longest lifetime of credentials an agent gets, e.g. "15m", for
profiles whose lifetime omnifob chooses (Cloudflare tokens, chained
and IAM users' roles, cross-partition roles, Google service
accounts). Longer ones are asked for with this lifetime and not
cached. At least 15 minutes, the shortest AWS session.

profiles.description:
Profile ids agents may get credentials for, as patterns in which `*`
stands for any characters within one `/`-separated segment, e.g.
`"acme/dev/*"` or `"*/*/ReadOnly"`. Unset, agents may use every profile.

enabled.description:
Append a line to `audit.jsonl` in the state directory for every
credential handed out: when, which profile, which command, which
agent, until when. Never the credentials.

Browser.description:
A browser, or one profile of a browser, that integrations open their
sign-ins and consoles in, so that each integration's sessions stay where
they belong.

command.description:
With `type = "command"`: the program and its arguments, run without a
shell; `{url}` in an argument is replaced by the URL, e.g.
`["flatpak", "run", "org.mozilla.firefox", "{url}"]`.

containers.description:
The colour and icon of the Firefox containers of the profiles each
entry matches, the first match winning (`isolate = "container"`).
Unmatched containers get the add-on's own.

engine.description:
With `type = "command"`: the engine the program's browser is built
on, which decides how its consoles can be kept apart. Without it,
they are not.

isolate.description:
How each AWS profile's console is kept apart from the others, so that
signing in as one does not sign the console out of another. Defaults
to what the browser supports: `profile` for Chromium-based browsers,
`container` for Firefox-based ones, `none` for the rest.

path.description:
Where the browser is, when fob does not find it on its own: an
absolute path (a macOS `.app` bundle or the program inside it), one
under `~/`, or a program name on `PATH`. Not for `command`.

profile.description:
The browser's own profile that sign-ins and other providers' consoles
open in: a Chromium profile folder, as `chrome://version` shows it
(`Default`, `Profile 1`), or a Firefox profile name. Not for
`command`.

type.description:
Which browser this is. fob finds the browsers it knows where they are
installed and knows how to open them; `command` runs any other
program.

BrowserType.description: The browsers fob knows, and `command` for any other.

oneOf.description: Google Chrome (Chromium).
Microsoft Edge (Chromium).
Brave (Chromium).
Vivaldi (Chromium).
Chromium, and ungoogled-chromium.
Helium (Chromium).
Thorium (Chromium).
Opera (Chromium); its consoles are not kept apart.
Arc (Chromium); its consoles are not kept apart.
Firefox, with its Developer Edition, Nightly and ESR (Gecko).
Zen (Gecko).
LibreWolf (Gecko).
Waterfox (Gecko).
Floorp (Gecko).
Safari (WebKit, macOS); its consoles are not kept apart.
Orion (WebKit, macOS); its consoles are not kept apart.
Any other program, given as `command`.

ChainedRole.description: A role assumed with the credentials of an Identity Center role.

duration.description:
Session length, 15 minutes to 1 hour (AWS caps role-chaining sessions
at one hour); defaults to one hour.

mfa_serial.description:
MFA device the role's trust policy requires (`mfa_serial` in
`~/.aws/config`); a code is asked for each new session.

region.description: Region exported for this role; defaults to the integration's.

session_name.description:
`RoleSessionName`; defaults to "omnifob", or "omnifob-agent" for
sessions a coding agent starts.

via_account_id.description: Account of the Identity Center role to start from.

via_role.description: Name of the Identity Center role (permission set) to start from.

ChainedRule.description:
One role name chained from a permission set in every account that has
it (`[integrations.<name>.chained_rules.<label>]`): discovery adds a
chained profile for each account where Identity Center lists `via_role`,
assuming `arn:<partition>:iam::<account>:role<path><role_name>` there.
Profiles are named like the account's Identity Center roles, with
`role_name` as the leaf.

accounts.description:
Only these accounts (12-digit IDs); every account with `via_role`
when empty.

duration.description:
Session length, 15 minutes to 1 hour (AWS caps role-chaining sessions
at one hour); defaults to one hour.

exclude_accounts.description: Accounts (12-digit IDs) the rule leaves out.

mfa_serial.description:
MFA device the roles' trust policies require; a code is asked for
each new session.

path.description: The role's IAM path, starting and ending with `/`; `/` unless set.

region.description: Region exported for these roles; defaults to the integration's.

role_name.description: Name of the IAM role to assume in each of those accounts.

session_name.description:
`RoleSessionName`; defaults to "omnifob", or "omnifob-agent" for
sessions a coding agent starts.

via_role.description:
Name of the Identity Center role (permission set) to start from; the
rule applies in every account where Identity Center gives it.

CloudflareTemplate.description:
A named set of permissions, written as they appear in the dashboard's API
names (e.g. "Workers Scripts Write"), never as IDs.

ips.description: Overrides the integration's `ips` for this template.

optional.description:
Permissions added when the account offers them and skipped otherwise,
for products that are new, renamed or not enabled everywhere.

r2_buckets.description:
R2 buckets that bucket-level permissions ("Workers R2 Storage Bucket
Item Write") apply to; "eu/name" for a bucket in a jurisdiction.

s3.description:
Also hand out the S3-compatible credentials R2 derives from the token
(`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3`).

zones.description:
Zones that zone-level permissions ("DNS Write") apply to, as domain
names ("example.com", looked up in the account when a token is
minted) or zone IDs. Empty means every zone in the account.

oneOf.description: Minted with a user-owned bootstrap token ("Create additional tokens").
Minted with an account-owned bootstrap token ("Account API Tokens Edit").

`{"env": {"NAME": "value", ...}, "expires_at": "<RFC 3339>"}`, with
`expires_at` optional; other keys are ignored.

The AWS `credential_process` format (`Version` 1, `AccessKeyId`,
`SecretAccessKey`, optional `SessionToken`, `Expiration` and
`AccountId`), exported as the AWS variables.

ContainerColor.description: The colours Firefox containers come in, as Granted Containers takes them.

ContainerIcon.description: The icons Firefox containers come with, as Granted Containers takes them.

ContainerStyle.description:
How the Firefox containers of some profiles look, e.g. red with a
fingerprint for `*/prod/*`.

profiles.description:
Profile ids this applies to, as patterns in which `*` stands for any
characters within one `/`-separated segment, as in `[agent]
profiles`.

CrossPartitionRole.description:
A role in another AWS partition, reached from an Identity Center role
(`[integrations.<name>.cross_partition.<label>]`): the Identity Center
role requests a web identity token with STS `GetWebIdentityToken` in its
own partition, and `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` exchanges it for the
role's credentials in the other partition. Checked when the config loads,
so `role_arn` is an IAM role ARN in a partition other than the source
Region's, and `region` is in the partition of `role_arn`.

audience.description:
The token's one audience: a client ID of the destination account's
OIDC provider for the source account's issuer.

duration.description:
Session length, 15 minutes to the destination role's maximum (at most
12 hours); defaults to one hour
([`CrossPartitionRole::DEFAULT_DURATION`]).

region.description: The destination partition's STS Region, exported as `AWS_REGION`.

role_arn.description: The role to assume, in another partition.

session_name.description:
`RoleSessionName`; defaults to "omnifob", or "omnifob-agent" for
sessions a coding agent starts.

signing_algorithm.description: How the token is signed; ES384 unless set.

source_region.description:
Where the token is requested; defaults to the integration's
`default_region`, then the portal's Region
([`CrossPartitionRole::source_region`]).

via_account_id.description: Account of the Identity Center role that requests the token.

via_role.description:
Name of the Identity Center role (permission set) that requests the
token.

Engine.description: The browser engine a browser is built on.

oneOf.description: Chromium (Blink): profiles, chosen with `--profile-directory`.

Mozilla's Gecko: Container Tabs, through the Granted Containers
add-on.
Apple's WebKit: nothing a command line can choose.

GcpServiceAccount.description:
A service account the signed-in account impersonates, which needs the
Service Account Token Creator role on it.

delegates.description:
Service accounts to go through, in order, when the account may only
impersonate this one by way of others.

lifetime.description:
Token lifetime; defaults to one hour, the most Google allows unless the
organization policy `iam.allowServiceAccountCredentialLifetimeExtension`
lists the account (then up to 12 hours).

project.description: Exported as the project; defaults to the one in the email.

scopes.description:
OAuth scopes for the token; defaults to cloud-platform and
userinfo.email, as gcloud asks.

IamRole.description: A role assumed with an IAM user's session.

console_duration.description:
How long `fob console` sessions last (`SessionDuration`), 15 minutes
to 12 hours and shorter than the role's maximum session duration.
Unset, a console session lasts as long as the role's credentials.

duration.description:
Session length, 15 minutes to 1 hour (STS counts a role assumed with
the user's `GetSessionToken` session as role chaining, which it caps
at one hour), or to 12 hours with `no_session`; defaults to one hour.

no_session.description:
Assume the role with the access key itself rather than the user's
session, as aws-vault's `--no-session` does: not role chaining, so
`duration` may be up to 12 hours (and up to the role's maximum
session duration). The user's `mfa_serial` code is then asked for
each new session of this role, and the key signs each `AssumeRole`.

region.description: Region exported for this role; defaults to the integration's.

session_name.description:
`RoleSessionName`; defaults to "omnifob", or "omnifob-agent" for
sessions a coding agent starts.

Integration.description:
The `type` values as written in the config file. Both Cloudflare types
share one configuration and differ only in how omnifob signs in.

browser.description:
The browser in `[browsers]` that this integration's sign-ins and
consoles open in; by default the system's.

chained.description:
Roles reached by assuming them from one of this portal's roles
(`role_arn` + `source_profile` in `~/.aws/config`), keyed by a label
that becomes the middle of the profile id.

chained_rules.description:
Roles chained the same way in every account where Identity Center
gives a permission set: one rule stands for a `chained` table per
account, and covers accounts added later. Keyed by a label of the
rule's own; profile ids take the account's segment and the role name.

console_duration.description:
How long `fob console` sessions of this portal's roles last
(`SessionDuration`), 15 minutes to 12 hours, and shorter than the
permission set's session duration, which omnifob cannot see. Unset,
a console session lasts as long as the role's credentials. Chained
roles cannot take it.

cross_partition.description:
Roles in another AWS partition, reached with a web identity token
that one of this portal's roles requests, keyed by a label that
becomes the middle of the profile id.

default_region.description: Region exported as `AWS_REGION` for every profile of this integration.

region.description: The region IAM Identity Center runs in.

scopes.description:
OIDC scopes. `sso:account:access` makes Identity Center issue a refresh
token, so sessions renew without a browser until the portal session ends.

start_url.description: The AWS access portal URL, e.g. `https://acme.awsapps.com/start`.

oneOf.description:
An IAM user's access key, kept in the keychain (`type = "aws-iam"`), the
way aws-vault keeps it. omnifob never hands the key out: it turns it into a
session with STS `GetSessionToken` (with an MFA code when `mfa_serial` is
set), and assumes `roles` with that session, which STS counts as role
chaining.

account.description: Middle segment of the session profile's id; defaults to the account ID.

browser.description:
The browser in `[browsers]` that this integration's sign-ins and
consoles open in; by default the system's.

mfa_serial.description:
The user's MFA device; sessions then carry MFA, which roles requiring
it accept.

region.description:
Region exported as `AWS_REGION` and used for STS; STS defaults to
us-east-1 when unset, and no region is exported.

roles.description:
Roles assumed with the user's session, keyed by a label that becomes
the middle of the profile id.

session_duration.description:
Length of the user's session, 15 minutes to 36 hours; defaults to
eight hours, a working day.

oneOf.description:
AWS console credentials (`type = "aws-login"`), as `aws login` gets
them: the browser signs in with a console session (an IAM user, the root
user or a federated role), and omnifob keeps a refresh token that renews
15 minute credentials for up to 12 hours, with no access key stored.

account.description: Middle segment of the profile's id; defaults to the account ID.

browser.description:
The browser in `[browsers]` that this integration's sign-ins and
consoles open in; by default the system's.

region.description:
The Region signed in through; the refresh token works only there. It
is also exported as `AWS_REGION` unless `default_region` is set.

roles.description:
Roles assumed with the console sign-in's credentials, keyed by a
label that becomes the middle of the profile id. STS counts these as
role chaining, so they last at most an hour.

oneOf.description:
A Google account (`type = "gcp"`), signed in the way `gcloud auth login`
signs in. Profiles are the account itself in each project, and service
accounts it may impersonate.

browser.description:
The browser in `[browsers]` that this integration's sign-ins and
consoles open in; by default the system's.

client_id.description:
An OAuth client of your own (a Desktop app client) instead of the one
gcloud ships. Both or neither.

projects.description:
The projects to offer; by default every active project the account
can see, listed at `fob sync`.

service_accounts.description:
Service accounts to impersonate, keyed by a label that becomes the
middle of the profile id.

oneOf.description:
A Microsoft Entra ID account (`type = "azure"`), signed in the way
`az login` signs in. Profiles are the account in each subscription.

browser.description:
The browser in `[browsers]` that this integration's sign-ins and
consoles open in; by default the system's.

subscriptions.description:
The subscriptions to offer (IDs); by default every one the account
can see, listed at `fob sync`.

tenant.description:
The tenant to sign in to (ID or domain); by default `organizations`,
which finds every tenant the account belongs to.

account_id.description:
Account to mint tokens for. When omitted, every account the bootstrap
token can list is discovered.

account_name.description: Display name for `account_id`; defaults to the ID.

browser.description:
The browser in `[browsers]` that this integration's sign-ins and
consoles open in; by default the system's.

client_id.description: `cloudflare-oauth`: the OAuth client to sign in with.

ips.description:
Addresses minted tokens may be used from, unless a template sets its
own: IPs or CIDR ranges, or "current" for this machine's public
addresses at minting time. Empty means anywhere.

scopes.description:
`cloudflare-oauth`: scopes requested at sign-in; defaults to the ones
minting needs.

session.description:
Sign-in session length. When set, `fob login` makes the new bootstrap
token expire after this long, so it works like an SSO session: a
stolen copy stops working, and a new one needs the dashboard sign-in.

templates.description: Extra templates, added to (or replacing) the built-in ones.

token_type.description:
The configured owner of minted tokens (`cloudflare-token` only). OAuth
leaves it at the default yet mints account-owned tokens, so code that
acts on the owner reads [`CloudflareConfig::minting`] instead.

ttl.description: Lifetime of minted tokens unless a template overrides it.

account_id.description:
Account to mint tokens for. When omitted, every account the bootstrap
token can list is discovered.

account_name.description: Display name for `account_id`; defaults to the ID.

browser.description:
The browser in `[browsers]` that this integration's sign-ins and
consoles open in; by default the system's.

client_id.description: `cloudflare-oauth`: the OAuth client to sign in with.

ips.description:
Addresses minted tokens may be used from, unless a template sets its
own: IPs or CIDR ranges, or "current" for this machine's public
addresses at minting time. Empty means anywhere.

scopes.description:
`cloudflare-oauth`: scopes requested at sign-in; defaults to the ones
minting needs.

session.description:
Sign-in session length. When set, `fob login` makes the new bootstrap
token expire after this long, so it works like an SSO session: a
stolen copy stops working, and a new one needs the dashboard sign-in.

templates.description: Extra templates, added to (or replacing) the built-in ones.

token_type.description:
The configured owner of minted tokens (`cloudflare-token` only). OAuth
leaves it at the default yet mints account-owned tokens, so code that
acts on the owner reads [`CloudflareConfig::minting`] instead.

ttl.description: Lifetime of minted tokens unless a template overrides it.

oneOf.description: Long-lived tokens for providers without short-lived credentials.

account.description: Middle segment of the profile id; defaults to "default".

browser.description:
The browser in `[browsers]` that this integration's sign-ins and
consoles open in; by default the system's.

preset.description: A known provider: its variable names, token check and console URL.

secrets.description:
Secret name → environment variables that receive it. It replaces the
preset's secrets and the fixed variables that come with them (such
as unikraft's `UNIKRAFT_PROFILE_ENV`); set those under `vars`.

vars.description: Non-secret variables exported along with the secrets.

verify_url.description:
URL that answers 2xx when the token is sent as a bearer token; it
needs exactly one secret, and replaces the preset's check.

oneOf.description:
An external program that prints credentials (`type = "command"`), such
as saml2aws, gimme-aws-creds, okta-aws-cli, AWS IAM Roles Anywhere's
`credential_process` helper or an in-house script. It is run without a
shell, its stderr passes through to the terminal (so it can prompt or
report), and its stdout is read as credentials: omnifob's own JSON
(`{"env": {...}, "expires_at": "<RFC 3339>"}`, as `fob creds` prints)
or the AWS `credential_process` format. Credentials with an expiry are
cached until then; credentials without one are fetched for each use.

account.description: Middle segment of the profile id; defaults to "default".

browser.description:
The browser in `[browsers]` that this integration's consoles open in;
by default the system's.

command.description:
The program and its arguments, run without a shell. The program is a
name looked up on `PATH`, an absolute path or one under `~/`.
`{ttl_seconds}` in an argument becomes the lifetime asked for, which
needs `ttl`.

console.description: URL `fob console` opens; there is none by default.

format.description:
What the program prints: `omnifob` (the default) or
`credential-process`.

name.description: Last segment of the profile id; defaults to the program's file name.

timeout.description:
How long the program may run before it is stopped, 1 second to 10
minutes; defaults to 2 minutes, enough for a browser sign-in.

ttl.description:
The lifetime to ask the program for, which makes it take `--ttl` and
`[agent] max_ttl`: passed as `{ttl_seconds}` in `command` and as
`OMNIFOB_TTL_SECONDS` in its environment. Unset, the program picks
the lifetime and `--ttl` is refused.

Isolation.description: How a browser keeps AWS consoles apart, one per fob profile.

oneOf.description:
A browser profile per fob profile (`--profile-directory`), which the
browser creates on first use. Chromium-based browsers.

A container (Firefox's Container Tabs) per fob profile, opened
through the Granted Containers add-on's `ext+granted-containers:`
URLs. Firefox-based browsers with the add-on.

Every console in the browser profile sign-ins open in, so signing in
as one AWS profile signs the console out of another.

Label.description:
Labels for the profiles matching `profiles`. For each label, the first
entry that matches a profile and sets it wins; profiles no entry labels
get what fob can tell or guess from their id.

access.description: What the profiles may do: "read", "write" or "admin".

env.description:
The environment, e.g. "prod", "staging" or "dev". `fob list` marks
"prod" and "production", and agents ask before using them.

profiles.description:
Profile ids this applies to, as patterns in which `*` stands for any
characters within one `/`-separated segment, e.g. `"acme/*-prd/*"`.

LoginRole.description:
A role assumed with the credentials of a console sign-in
(`[integrations.<name>.roles.<label>]` of an `aws-login` integration).

duration.description:
Session length, 15 minutes to 1 hour (AWS caps role-chaining
sessions at one hour); defaults to one hour.

mfa_serial.description:
MFA device the role's trust policy requires; a code is asked for
each new session.

region.description: Region exported for this role; defaults to the integration's.

session_name.description:
`RoleSessionName`; defaults to "omnifob", or "omnifob-agent" for
sessions a coding agent starts.

SigningAlgorithm.description:
The algorithm `GetWebIdentityToken` signs the token with
(`SigningAlgorithm`).

oneOf.description: ECDSA with P-384 and SHA-384, the one AWS's examples use.
RSA with SHA-256, for relying parties without ECDSA.

agent.description: What commands run by a coding agent may use.

audit.description: The local audit log of credentials handed out.

browsers.description:
Browsers, or profiles of one browser, that integrations open in,
keyed by the name their `browser` key refers to.

directories.description:
Default profiles per directory: a directory (absolute, or starting
with `~/`) and the id of the profile that `fob exec` and `fob use`
pick in it, and in every directory below it, when no profile is
named. The longest matching directory wins.

labels.description:
The environment and access level of profiles, by pattern, which
`fob list` shows; profiles no entry labels get guesses from their id.
